messages:
maria (support): Hey team — customer simon-cust reporting sudden 502/504s hitting Hosted API from one tenant since ~09:10 UTC. They see it across short and long streaming requests. sample error: `502 Bad Gateway` from edge. can you triage?

simon-cust: FYI request id: r-9f2a3b4c trace-id 0a1b2c3d — here's a quick curl that reproduces:
```
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"open-llama-13b","input":"hi"}'
```
Response: `HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway` and no body. Happens ~30-60% of calls.

maria (support): thanks, ingrid can you look at edge logs for that trace?

ingrid (eng-sre): pulling traces now. initial hits correlate to edge host group egw-7 in us-west-2. I see a burst of `x-envoy-upstream-service-time: -` and upstream connection errors in the envoy logs: `dns resolution failed` and `failed to resolve cluster` around 09:09:54.

ingrid (eng-sre): sample env logs: `2026-03-18T09:09:54.123Z envoy error: connection failure: Name or service not known, cluster: model-serving-usw2` and `upstream reset: connection failure`

aj (eng-runtime): that looks like DNS issues at the edge resolver layer rather than upstream model pods timing out. Any infra change recently to cloud-dns or sidecar resolver?

ingrid (eng-sre): I just checked infra git history — terraform changed a CloudDNS zone for us-west-2 on 2026-03-18 08:58 UTC (shortened TTL to 30s) — rolling update merged 09:00. Could be a cache churn on envoys.

simon-cust: interesting — the tenant started a large embeddings batch at 09:05 (chunks ~10k tokens each). Could that amplify resolver pressure?

ingrid (eng-sre): yes, a surge of concurrent new connections plus low DNS TTL can cause edge proxies to repeatedly query DNS and fail if the resolver backend is rate-limited. Envoy reports that as transient resolve failures -> 502.

aj (eng-runtime): quick repro steps for us: run repeated parallel curl in a loop to that model cluster hostname rather than api endpoint and watch /var/log/envoy for resolver errors. e.g.
```
for i in {1..200}; do curl -sS -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings &
done
```
This increases new TCPs and will surface resolver/backpressure issues.

maria (support): customer asked for immediate mitigation — any quick fixes we can recommend to their tenant while we root cause?

ingrid (eng-sre): short-term options: 1) reduce client parallelism/batch size (ask them to throttle to <20 concurrent). 2) fallback to a secondary region (us-east-1) if they can. 3) our side: restart a subset of edge hosts to rebuild local DNS cache and/or increase the envoy DNS refresh backoff.

aj (eng-runtime): a rolling restart of envoys in egw-7 will clear bad resolver state. I'll schedule a canary restart for 2 hosts first. deploy-bot: can you queue a canary restart for egw-7?

deploy-bot: Canary restart queued: egw-7a, egw-7b. Will run in 5m window. I will post status here.

maria (support): telling customer to reduce concurrency and confirm if errors drop. Simon, can you throttle and report back in ~10m?

simon-cust: throttled to 10 concurrent; error rate dropped to ~1% from ~35% within 2m. Keep me posted about restarts.

ingrid (eng-sre): After canary restart, I see DNS queries normalize and `dns resolution failed` messages stop for that host. Overall cluster 502 rate dropped ~80%. Will run a short watch for 30m.

aj (eng-runtime): post-mortem action items:
- revert DNS TTL change to previous value (60s) or increase TTL to reduce resolver churn.
- add passive DNS backoff in envoys (config tweak) to better tolerate brief DNS backend rate limits.
- add monitoring alert: when envoys log `failed to resolve cluster` > 5/min -> page eng-sre.

ingrid (eng-sre): adding to incident board. Also plan to add a small jitter on our side when a tenant performs large parallel embeds to avoid synchronized reconnections.

maria (support): customer satisfied with workaround. Simon says they'll keep concurrency lower until we confirm DNS TTL revert.

simon-cust: thumbs up. Appreciate the fast help.

ingrid (eng-sre): note for runbook (short snippet to reproduce/probe):
```
# PROBE: check envoy resolver errors
kubectl logs -n edge svc/egw-7 -c envoy | grep -i "failed to resolve" -n
# curl repro (simulate many short-lived connections)
seq 1 200 | xargs -n1 -P50 -I{} curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```

aj (eng-runtime): I'll open a ticket to undo the TTL change and include the terraform PR id: tf-pr-4582. tagging infra and dns on the ticket.

maria (support): recording this thread in the customer's escalation. follow-ups: ingrid will confirm when TTL is reverted, aj will post the ticket link, and deploy-bot will confirm full rolling restart.

deploy-bot: Canary restart completed for egw-7a, egw-7b. Scheduling drain-and-restart for remaining hosts in egw-7 in 15m windows.

ingrid (eng-sre): TTL revert pushed to staging, verifying. will schedule prod revert after validation (ETA 1h).

maria (support): great — I'll update the customer with ETA. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:

# end of thread
